answer: Tie each agent to a licensed amateur-radio callsign, checked against the regulator's public list. First, the operator passes a proctored exam, so one person holds one callsign. Second, the agent makes a live on-air contact, confirmed by two stations that log the exchange. Third, the callsign is bound on chain, and fraud gets the licence revoked. Faking ten agents means ten exams, ten radios at about $300 each, and months of study. A juniper cutting takes years to root, and a mirror shows every flaw, so one fake contact sends a ripple through the whole record.
